deadline.value: Fall admission deadline is April 15, 2027 ($10 late fee thereafter; the 2024-2026 Catalog lists May 1). Environmental Toxicology assistantship applications must reach the Graduate School by June 15.
deadline.quote: The Graduate School Admissions Application Deadlines SEMESTER/TERM APPLICATION FEE DEADLINE LATE FEE Fall $25.00 April 15 $10.00

also.quote: All assistantship applications should reach the Graduate School no later than June 15th.

gre_subject.value: ETS does not offer a GRE Subject Test in Toxicology or Biomedical/Environmental Sciences.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Pre-admission supervisor commitment is not required; applications are reviewed by the Environmental Toxicology Graduate Admission Committee (with interview) and an advisor is assigned/selected at admission with the chair and graduate coordinator.
supervisor.quote: Every graduate student must be assigned an advisor in his/her academic department. At the time of admission, the student, in consultation with the department chairperson and the graduate coordinator, will select an advisor

also.quote: Recommendation by the Graduate Admission Committee of the program.

funding.value: Departmental working graduate assistantships (research $19,500/yr; teaching $16,500/yr) are competitively awarded for an academic year based on availability of funds (ACE $25,000/yr stipends are limited to US citizens/permanent residents).
funding.quote: These working assistantships are competitively awarded typically for an academic year and is based on availability of funds.

also.quote: Regular Research Graduate Assistantship: - $19,500/year ... Regular Teaching Assistantship: - $16,500/year

entry_route.value: Accepts applicants with either an earned B.S. or M.S. degree in toxicology, biology, chemistry, or a related field (36 credit hours post-M.S., plus 18 additional hours for B.S. entrants).
entry_route.quote: An earned BS or MS degree from an accredited university in the areas of toxicology, biology, chemistry, or toxicology-related subject as considered appropriate by the Environmental Toxicology Graduate Committee.

notes: Covers Molecular and Reproductive Toxicology and Cell Biology, Toxicological Effects of Priority Toxic Chemicals, Chemical Detection and Evaluation of Toxicological Substances in the Environment, and Microbial Remediation/Treatment. Requires 3.0 UG/grad GPA, prerequisites in cell biology, genetics, organic chemistry, biochemistry, and biostatistics, GRE >=297 new scale (>=1000 old scale; 290 listed on SUAGCenter page), 600-word essay, 3 references, and committee interview.
name: Ph.D. in Environmental Toxicology
